top_choice_rationale: P002 is the most mature and decisive achievement on the slate: the Higgs boson, predicted in 1964 and observed in 2012 by two independent detectors, with a decade of coupling and mass measurements; the 2013 prize honoured the theory, not the observation. The citation names both ATLAS and CMS and rests on conception and construction leadership, a stateable rule, though the three-name cut across two collaborations is the weakest allocation and my instrument-building background makes me discount my own preference. If that rule is not accepted, the mixed or experimental optical-lattice proposals (P004, P005) are the best fallbacks, then the clean two-name optical clock (P001), then the younger moire field (P003), with no award last.
recusal_note: No documented tie to any credited person; my detector and collaboration background (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+) is a disclosed instrumentalist bias toward P002, not a conflict requiring recusal.
